page: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is a compute-oriented virtual machine from the Dldsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at a high clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is provided via a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD, and the CPU includes a large 480 MB L3 cache alongside advanced instruction sets like AVX-512, AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions), and Intel Deep Learning Boost.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression reaching 36.23 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 14.92 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling is limited, as evidenced by a weak stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 4655.9 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 29.51 GB/sec. Memory performance is balanced, with a read-only small block bandwidth of 345.13 GB/sec, though large block write bandwidth is weaker at 23.53 GB/sec. The server handles lightweight LLM inference adequately, processing 634.3 tokens/sec for a small 135M model, but struggles with larger 7B models.

Given its dedicated high-frequency CPU cores and integrated NVMe storage, the D4lds_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require large memory footprints. The low memory density represents a clear tradeoff, making it unsuitable for large-scale databases or memory-intensive applications. It is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, lightweight web serving, microservices, and basic batch processing where high clock speed and fast local storage are prioritized over memory capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure D4lds_v7 is a compute-focused virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs (2 physical cores), 8.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 236 GB local NVMe SSD. The server features a substantial 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Benchmarks show strong single-threaded performance, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression scoring in the top tier, though multi-core scaling and write memory bandwidth are relatively weak. With a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this instance is optimized for CPU-bound, low-memory workloads. It is highly suitable for single-threaded processing, lightweight web serving, and microservices that benefit from high clock speeds and fast local storage.
